name: Rover lunaire (LRV)
tagline: I am the first electric car ever driven on the Moon.
discovery: By driving about 28 km, I let the astronauts travel much farther than on foot and collect very old rocks, including the famous "Genesis Rock", about 4 billion years old.
status_note: Parked forever near the landing site. Two other rovers like me are parked on the Moon (Apollo 16 and 17).

presentation.title: Hello, I'm Rover lunaire (LRV).
presentation.body: I'm a rover from the Apollo 15 mission. I am the first electric car ever driven on the Moon.

chapters.title: Folded like origami
chapters.body: For the trip, I was folded up and stowed on the side of the lunar module Falcon. Once there, astronauts David Scott and James Irwin pull on straps and I unfold.

chapters.title: Driving on the Moon
chapters.body: Each of my four wheels has its own electric motor, powered by batteries. My tyres are made of woven wire mesh: an air-filled tyre would not have survived the vacuum and the extreme temperatures. I drive at a little over 10 km/h through the dust.

chapters.title: My last job: filming the departure
chapters.body: Before leaving, the astronauts park me a little way off with my camera on. From Earth, engineers use it to film the ascent stage lifting off. Then I stay there, parked forever.

quiz.question: Why were the lunar rover's tyres not filled with air?
choices: To withstand the vacuum and extreme temperatures
quiz.explanation: On the Moon there is no air, and the temperature changes enormously between day and night. Metal mesh holds up better.

quiz.question: How many lunar rovers are parked on the Moon?
quiz.explanation: One for each of the Apollo 15, 16 and 17 missions.
